definitions.gloss: casual speech, informal language between equals
definitions.explanation: Informal, plain-form speech used between people of equal status (same age, close friends, etc.). Contrasted with {敬語|けいご} (polite/formal language).

examples.japanese: タメ{語|ご}で{話|はな}していいよ。
examples.english: You can talk to me casually.

examples.japanese: {先輩|せんぱい}にタメ{語|ご}を{使|つか}うのは{失礼|しつれい}だ。
examples.english: Using casual speech with a senior is rude.

examples.japanese: {同|おな}い{年|どし}だとわかったので、タメ{語|ご}に{切|き}り{替|か}えた。
examples.english: Once I found out we were the same age, I switched to casual speech.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
タメ comes from gambling slang where タメ means "equal" (as in dice showing the same number). {語|ご} means "language/speech." So タメ{語|ご} literally means "equal-status language."

USAGE:
The shift from {敬語|けいご} to タメ{語|ご} is an important social milestone in Japanese relationships. Being invited to use タメ{語|ご} signals closeness and acceptance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- タメ{語|ご}で{話|はな}す: to speak casually
- タメ{語|ご}を{使|つか}う: to use casual speech
- タメ{語|ご}に{切|き}り{替|か}える: to switch to casual speech
- タメ{語|ご}でいい: casual speech is fine
